description: We are an engineering team combining aerospace design, data architecture, and systems engineering. For this challenge, we leverage NASA Mars datasets to build an interactive tool for surface EVA operations, supported by a rotary-wing UAV and an autonomous rover concept tailored for low gravity and harsh terrain to capture multi-angle spatial data.
summary:
Our project is about making Mars exploration safer and easier for astronauts. We are designing a system that uses NASA satellite data, a rover, and a drone connected to the rover with a cable.

First, the system studies Mars maps and creates a safe route for the rover. It also selects places where the drone will fly and scan the surface. While moving, the rover checks its surroundings for possible dangers. If it finds an unexpected obstacle, such as a large trench, it stops and sends the drone to collect more information. Then, the system updates the map and finds a new route.

Our system also helps astronauts by showing safe walking paths, good places for observation, and interesting areas for scientific research.

We believe this project can make future Mars missions safer and help astronauts explore more areas with better information.
details:
Our project aims to make Mars exploration safer, easier, and more useful for astronauts. We designed a system that combines NASA satellite data, a rover, and a drone connected to the rover with a cable. These parts work together to explore the surface, find possible dangers, search for useful resources, and create safe routes for both the rover and astronauts.

Our system has several important functions:

1. Surface Mapping and Route Planning

First, the system uses satellite images and terrain data to study the Martian surface. It creates a map that shows different terrain types, possible dangers, and interesting areas.

  • It identifies safe and unsafe areas for rover movement.
  • It creates the main route for the rover.
  • It selects special points where the drone will take off and scan the area.
  • It can update the route when new information is collected.

2. Surface and Underground Exploration

Our project focuses on both surface and underground exploration. We want to help astronauts find useful areas and possible natural resources on Mars.

  • Surface scans help us understand the terrain, rocks, slopes, and possible obstacles.
  • Underground scanning data can help identify interesting geological structures.
  • Different data layers can be used to find possible mineral and resource areas.
  • The system helps select locations that may be useful for future scientific research.

3. Rover and Drone Cooperation

The rover and drone work together during the mission. The rover moves on the ground, while the drone provides a wider view of the surrounding area.

  • The rover continuously checks its nearby environment for possible dangers.
  • The drone performs detailed scans at planned points.
  • It can also take off when the rover finds an unexpected obstacle.
  • The drone collects new information and sends it to the system.
  • The rover uses this information to continue safely.

4. Automatic Hazard Detection and Route Updates

One of the main features of our project is that the rover does not have to follow the same route in every situation.

For example, if the rover detects a large trench or an unsafe area, it stops immediately. The drone then flies above the area and collects more information. After this scan, the system updates the map and calculates a new route.

This makes the mission more flexible and helps the rover avoid dangerous areas.

5. Astronaut Safety and Walking Routes

Our project also considers the safety of astronauts, not only the rover.

  • It creates safe walking routes for astronauts.
  • It identifies suitable hills and high places for observation.
  • It marks interesting locations for scientific experiments.
  • It helps astronauts explore areas that have already been checked by the rover and drone.

The rover and astronaut team can move together in a planned way. While the rover travels to the next scanning point, astronauts can explore an area that was checked before.

6. Information Sharing and Mission Control

All collected information is brought together in a central system. This information can be shared with astronauts through tablets and helmet displays.

Astronauts can see updated maps, safe routes, possible dangers, scanning results, and scientific targets. This helps them understand the environment and make better decisions during the mission.

What Makes Our Project Different?

The main idea of our project is to bring mapping, surface and underground exploration, resource research, rover movement, drone scanning, and astronaut safety together in one system.

Instead of using a fixed route, our system can change its plans when new information appears. The rover and drone support each other, while the collected data also helps astronauts plan their own exploration.

Our goal is to create a system that can make future Mars missions safer, more organized, and more successful.
